title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Field Shape Verification
verification_method: Focused S18P2 preferred_address requirement-home tests, adjacent preferred-address migration and transport-parameter fuzz regression tests, existing transport-parameter benchmark scenarios, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, Release build, full Release test suite, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers selected preferred_address transport-parameter field-shape requirements and the bounded S18P2 server-address cutover pointer after preferred-address validation succeeds.
expected_result: The focused tests show that preferred_address preserves both address families and both ports, accepts an all-zero unused family only when those fields are still present, writes network-byte-order IP address bytes, writes two-byte port fields, preserves the associated stateless reset token as the final 16-byte field, rejects truncated preferred_address values, keeps the original server address before preferred-address validation, and promotes to the preferred server address after validation succeeds.
procedure: Run the focused S18P2 preferred_address requirement-home filter.
Run the adjacent preferred-address migration and transport-parameter fuzz regression filter.
Run the full Release test suite without rebuilding.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The transport-parameter codec accepts and emits RFC 9000 Section 18.2 transport-parameter tuples.
The existing preferred-address path validation flow remains available.
The permanent QuicTransportParametersBenchmarks suite includes server preferred_address parse and format scenarios.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim preferred_address connection-ID sequence/accounting constraints, disable_active_migration exception behavior, full S9.6 migration lifecycle closure, public migration APIs, multipath behavior, or hosted interop readiness.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-05. The Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the focused S18P2 preferred_address requirement-home filter passed 14/14, the adjacent preferred-address migration and transport-parameter fuzz regression filter passed 5/5, regenerated coverage triage marks the selected ten S18P2 requirements trace_clean and reports 1,243 of 1,771 QUIC requirements trace-clean overall, core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 433 artifacts, the full Release no-build suite passed 4,440/4,440, and git diff --check returned exit code 0 with line-ending warnings only.
